verdicts.title: Serialization docs promise InputTypeError for an unregistered leaf; the code raises a bare TypeError, and the regression test cannot tell the difference
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified in the current tree and reproduced at runtime. (1) packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/serialization/_structural.py:38-47 `_unrecognized_leaf` is annotated `-> TypeError` and returns `TypeError(...)`; it is raised at :79 (save) and :114 (restore). No import of opaque.exceptions exists in that module, and the dispatcher (_dispatch.py) does not translate it -- _walk_load only adds an exception note for *registered* handlers, and the structural path is reached after `resolve_serializer` misses. (2) docs/reference/serialization.md:17-20 states the leaf 'raises `InputTypeError` on both save and restore'. `git show 7b26f655` (feat(exceptions): add public exception taxonomy, #760) changed exactly that word from `TypeError` to `InputTypeError` with no source change under packages/opaque-base/src, while the sibling sentence on the same page (shape mismatch -> `CheckpointError`) *was* backed by code: packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/serialization/_structural.py:38 imports CheckpointError and raises it at :52 and :67. So this is an incomplete conversion, not a carve-out. (3) InputTypeError is `class InputTypeError(OpaqueError, TypeError)` (packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/exceptions/__init__.py:31-32), i.e. a *subclass* of TypeError, so `except InputTypeError` cannot catch a bare TypeError and `except OpaqueError` cannot either. Reproduced with PYTHONPATH=packages/opaque-base/src: `state_dict(Foo())` and `from_state_dict(Foo(), {})` both raise plain `TypeError` (MRO: TypeError -> Exception), `isinstance(e, opaque.exceptions.OpaqueError) is False`, `isinstance(e, InputTypeError) is False`. (4) The only guarding test, packages/opaque-base/tests/serialization/test_fail_closed_dispatch.py:64-80, asserts `pytest.raises(TypeError, match='Cannot serialize'/'Cannot restore')`, which passes identically for both exception types, so CI does not hold the documented contract. (5) The stale prose also persists in code: packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/serialization/__init__.py:7-9 and _dispatch.py:7 both still say `TypeError`. Searched for any wrapper or translation layer between the structural walker and the public facade and found none. Downgraded from medium to low: docs/reference/exceptions.md does advertise `OpaqueError` for 'any semantic Opaque failure', so the taxonomy promise is genuinely broken, but the behavior is fail-closed in every direction -- nothing is silently dropped, no epsilon is affected, and the worst outcome is an uncaught TypeError instead of a caught one. No open tracked issue covers it (#775/#845 are the citation-sweep umbrella and its citation child, not exception-taxonomy drift).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A caller writes the handler the exceptions page invites -- `try: state = from_state_dict(template, torch.load(path)) except CheckpointError: abort_resume() except InputTypeError: report_unregistered_type()`, or a coarser `except OpaqueError` resume/start-fresh switch -- around a state tree that contains a leaf with no registered serializer and no generic-container shape (a custom optimizer-state object, a third-party schedule handle). Reproduced: both `opaque.serialization.state_dict(obj)` and `opaque.serialization.from_state_dict(obj, {})` raise a bare `TypeError('Cannot serialize/restore ...')`, for which `isinstance(exc, InputTypeError)` and `isinstance(exc, OpaqueError)` are both False, so neither documented handler fires and the resume path crashes with an unhandled TypeError instead of taking its fallback branch. Impact is limited to error-handling ergonomics: the operation still fails closed, no state is silently dropped, and no privacy parameter is affected. The one CI test that covers the path (test_fail_closed_dispatch.py:64-80) matches on `TypeError`, so it passes before and after the intended conversion and pins nothing.

verdicts.title: apply_runtime_patches / apply_model_patches swallow ImportError raised inside the patch application, and is_runtime_patched() reports True when nothing was installed
verdicts.reasoning: Mechanics all verified in the current tree and the two headline behaviors reproduced with the repo venv (torch 2.14.0+cu130, transformers 5.15.1, peft 0.20.0). (a) packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/__init__.py:63-76 puts the `apply_transformers_model_patches(model, ...)` CALL inside the same `try` as its import and swallows ImportError at logger.debug('opaque: Hugging Face kernel patches not available.'); :78-86 does the same for PEFT with a bare `pass`. A detail that strengthens the claim: both symbols are already imported unconditionally at module scope (:12-13), so the inner imports are sys.modules hits that cannot fail -- the `except ImportError` can ONLY ever catch an ImportError raised from inside the patch call. Reproduced: registering a family via `register_family('fakefam', fn_raising_ImportError)` and calling `apply_model_patches(model, compat=True)` on a PreTrainedModel with `config.model_type == 'fakefam'` returns normally, logs only the DEBUG line, and leaves the model unpatched (the apply_fn was entered once). #899's ConfigurationError at _router.py:141-148 does not fire because the family IS registered. (b) :101-102 sets `_runtime_patches_applied = True` before any of the four per-concern blocks; :109-137 each wrap their call in `except ImportError: pass` with no log (only the vmap_checkpointing block at :139-149 logs a warning). Reproduced: `apply_runtime_patches(performance=False, compat=False)` installs nothing yet `is_runtime_patched()` returns True while the sibling `opaque.api.patches.torch.is_checkpoint_patched()` correctly returns False -- the correct pattern at torch/checkpoint/__init__.py:42-61 sets its flag only after the applies succeed. (c) The two silent `except ImportError: return` sites are real: _family.py:200-203 and _factory.py:283-286. _router.py:59-91 `_patch_forward` returns False silently when `target_cls is None`. Two corrections to the finding's framing, which is why I am not rating this higher. First, its stated 'realistic trigger' is misattributed: HF symbol drift does NOT reach the facade's ImportError swallow -- the symbol replacements in _family.py are `hasattr(mod, 'repeat_kv')` / `hasattr(mod, 'eager_attention_forward')` guarded and the modeling-module import is caught locally, so drift manifests as the _family/_factory silent skip, not as a swallowed ImportError. Every component import in _factory.py is top-level (:28-63), and the Triton kernel imports in components/*.py are inside the patched forward, not the apply, so with shipped families the (a) swallow is effectively unreachable today; I confirmed all 26 shipped `_MODULE_PATH` values import cleanly under transformers 5.15.1 (0 failures). The reachable trigger is the documented downstream extension point (`register_family`), which is how I reproduced it. Second, leg (c) is weak on its own: the docstring's summary line at :153 says 'True once apply_runtime_patches has run in this interpreter', which is exactly what it reports; only the trailing sentence overclaims 'whether the global shims are installed'. This same leg was already attacked and rejected in this audit's own earlier pass (.audit-checkpoint/NEW-FINDINGS-MASTER-LIST.md:690, item 9). Net: a genuine latent fail-open in a public extension path plus a misleading predicate, no current-version defect, no epsilon impact -> low. Not covered by any open tracked issue (#813 is parity xfails; the perf-audit patches issues are unrelated).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Reproduced on the current tree: a downstream user follows the documented extension path in opaque/api/patches/transformers/_registry.py (`register_family(name, apply_fn)`) and their apply_fn raises ImportError because an internal transformers symbol it reaches for has moved. `opaque.patches.apply_model_patches(model, compat=True)` returns normally, emits only `DEBUG opaque: Hugging Face kernel patches not available.`, and the model keeps its un-vmap-safe attention path -- #899's ConfigurationError cannot fire because the family is registered. Also reproduced: `apply_runtime_patches(performance=False, compat=False)` installs nothing yet `opaque.patches.is_runtime_patched()` returns True (the flag is set at __init__.py:102 before any block runs), while `opaque.api.patches.torch.is_checkpoint_patched()` correctly returns False, so no public API can distinguish 'entry point called' from 'shims installed'. For the SHIPPED families this is latent, not active: all 26 registered modeling modules import cleanly under the installed transformers 5.15.1, and a future in-range 5.x symbol move would be dropped by the hasattr guards in _family.py:207-226 or the local `except ImportError: return` at _family.py:200-203 / _factory.py:283-286 rather than by the facade's swallow -- in every one of those paths the only signal is silence or a DEBUG line, and the same fail-open that #899 closed for unregistered families stays open for registered ones.

verdicts.title: Stale 'bound' entry in the trainer mechanism-kwargs allowlist makes the error message advertise a kwarg that a second check rejects
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_training_arguments.py:228-229 still has `'gaussian': frozenset({'bound', 'compute_dtype'})` in `_MECHANISM_KWARGS`, consumed at :1360-1365 by `_validate_privacy_kwargs`, whose message (:282-289) renders `Allowed: {sorted(allowed)}`. :1222-1228 unconditionally rejects `'bound' in self.privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs` with ConfigurationError('... Opaque does not provide a matching privacy accountant.'). Commit provenance checks out: 873de427 'delete(dpsgd)!: remove unsupported bounded Gaussian noise (#1021)' added the bound rejection (and removed the doc comment mentioning 'bound for the bounded Gaussian mechanism'), and b9b0a23e 'fix(transformers)!: validate privacy kwargs (#1024)' introduced _MECHANISM_KWARGS carrying 'bound' forward. Reproduced with the repo venv: TrainingArguments(..., privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs={'nope': 1.0}) -> "privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs contains unsupported keys for privacy_noise_mechanism='gaussian': ['nope']. Allowed: ['bound', 'compute_dtype']." and privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs={'bound': 1.0} -> "privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs['bound'] is unsupported: Opaque does not provide a matching privacy accountant." Note the ordering the finding does not spell out: the bound rejection at :1222 runs BEFORE the allowlist at :1360, so 'bound' can never slip through the allowlist -- the allowlist entry is pure dead text that only ever appears inside an error message. Severity is already low and stays low: both paths fail closed, nothing is mis-trained, and no privacy parameter is affected; the defect is a self-contradicting diagnostic on a privacy surface. No open tracked issue covers it.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user passes an unrecognized mechanism kwarg (e.g. privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs={'nope': 1.0}) with the default privacy_noise_mechanism='gaussian'. Reproduced message: "privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs contains unsupported keys for privacy_noise_mechanism='gaussian': ['nope']. Allowed: ['bound', 'compute_dtype']." -- advertising `bound`, the bounded-Gaussian knob deliberately deleted in #1021 for having no matching privacy accountant. If the user then sets it, the earlier guard at _training_arguments.py:1222-1228 raises "privacy_noise_mechanism_kwargs['bound'] is unsupported". Because that guard runs before the allowlist, `bound` is never actually accepted, so there is no mis-training or privacy consequence at all: the only defect is that an error message on a privacy-configuration surface names a removed, accountant-less noise knob as allowed. Cosmetic/diagnostic only.

verdicts.title: docs/user-guide/distributed.md advertises six opaque.distributed helpers that have no public import path
verdicts.reasoning: Fully verified. docs/user-guide/distributed.md:261 is the section heading '## `opaque.distributed` API summary' and its table (269-288) lists reduce_scalar (:278), gather_tensors (:281), gather_pytree (:282), assert_pytree_equal (:283), sync_object (:285) and assert_scalar_equal (:286). packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/distributed/__init__.py:31-48 declares __all__ = all_reduce, barrier, gather_for_metrics, get_rank, get_world_size, is_distributed, is_main_process, local_shard, num_processes, process_index, reduce_pytree, reduce_pytree_, sum_gradients, sum_gradients_, sync, wait_for_everyone -- none of the six. The two documented power-user submodules do not carry them either: opaque/distributed/collectives.py exports only all_reduce, all_reduce_, barrier, get_rank, get_world_size, is_distributed, and opaque/distributed/gradients.py only reduce_pytree(_), sum_gradients(_). Probed at runtime in the repo venv: hasattr is False for all six on opaque.distributed, opaque.distributed.collectives and opaque.distributed.gradients (all_reduce_ is indeed reachable, via collectives only). The six exist solely at packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/distributed/_state.py:40 assert_scalar_equal, :90 assert_pytree_equal, :123 reduce_scalar, :311 gather_tensors, :321 gather_pytree, :391 sync_object; the internal aggregator opaque/api/engine/distributed/__init__.py re-exports only sync and register_sync_type from that module, so there is no opaque.api.* public-ish path either. docs/reference/distributed.md carries 11 ':::' identifiers and none of the six, so the two doc pages also disagree. Severity stays low: the failure is a plain ImportError at author time, fail-closed, no epsilon or numerical impact; the substantive part is that the DDP equivalence self-check the guide points at (assert_pytree_equal) is not performable through a supported path, an ARC-003 documentation-vs-code inconsistency. Not a duplicate of any open tracked issue (#775/#845 are the citation sweep).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user following the user guide's '`opaque.distributed` API summary' table writes `from opaque.distributed import assert_pytree_equal` (or reduce_scalar / gather_tensors / gather_pytree / sync_object / assert_scalar_equal) to check that DDP ranks hold identical noised gradients, and gets ImportError -- verified: hasattr is False for all six on opaque.distributed and on both documented power-user submodules (opaque.distributed.collectives, opaque.distributed.gradients). The only place they exist is the private opaque.api.engine.distributed._state module, which is not re-exported by opaque/api/engine/distributed/__init__.py either. Consequence is confined to documentation: an author-time ImportError with no runtime, numerical, or privacy effect, plus the fact that the guide's suggested cross-rank equivalence self-check has no supported import path and docs/reference/distributed.md omits all six.
